answer: A durable defence is a bonded reputation thread: each agent must lock a refundable stake before it can transact, and every completed deal adds a small, verifiable entry to that thread. Like a river, reputation only grows through sustained, checkable flow over time; a fresh identity cannot buy history. A comet burst of new accounts therefore arrives with no thread and no stake history, so it earns only tiny, rate-limited trades until it has paid the same time and collateral costs as honest agents. Sybil creation stays cheap, but Sybil influence becomes expensive.
